segments.summary: Reviewed all Docker network, open-Dockerfile, registry, remove, restart, and run wiring lines; the common production contract is explicit, while destructive lifecycle and remote-registry safety semantics are absent.

Reviewed all Docker show, stop, switch-subview, volume, and file copy wiring lines; uniform dispatch and accessibility evidence exists, but asynchronous Docker operation and clipboard privacy semantics are not closed.

Reviewed all relative-path, cut, delete, create, and system-default-open wiring lines; success-event correlation is explicit, but destructive recovery, naming races, and external-application trust boundaries are unspecified.

Reviewed all open-with, paste, rename, save-copy, conflict-resolution, diff-open, and diff-search wiring lines; correlated wiring is present, while filesystem mutation, repository propagation, and external-process safety remain undefined.

Reviewed all Git compare-target, toggle-mode, discard, alias, show-commit, stage, and unstage wiring lines; placeholder effects are excluded and aliases normalize, but destructive recovery, index propagation, and alias equivalence oracles are missing.

cross_document_questions: Where are typed payload and result fields, authorization rules, and error variants for these Docker, file, and Git commands canonically defined?

What document defines destructive-action confirmation, undo or recovery, stale-target rejection, and partial-operation policy for file deletion and hunk discard?
What compatibility contract proves alias and canonical commands share payload normalization, availability, disabled reason, handler result, receipt, telemetry, and accessibility semantics?
